story: On a breezy, clear Saturday afternoon in Sumter Oaks, Gary putters around his house while content as ever, not far from the street. Over on Magnolia Loop, Donna is cheerful as she promises Rosa her deviled eggs for Friday's supper at six, teasing that the extra flamingos are already hidden behind the hedge. Hal, dutifully counting the pink birds against the community's three-ornament limit, looks less amused, while warm and amused Rosa tells Donna not to let Hal rattle her and that they'll sort out the flamingo problem over supper.
events: Gary waited: puttering around Gary's House
Hal (donna flamingo flock): Count the street-visible flamingos against the three-ornament limit

gary.thought_process: Lunch is made and the toolbox is sorted. The lights and speakers are tested and still waiting on Architectural Review approval, and I filed that request with the 10 PM cutoff noted. Rosa's dinner is tonight and I promised cornbread. I checked the fridge last tick but never confirmed the cornmeal and buttermilk, and I'd hate to show up empty-handed. The workbench is where I'd do a final once-over on the connectors so the cart is ready the moment approval comes through, and it keeps me busy and useful. Everything stays garage-side, out of the street's view, so L-01 isn't a problem until approval.
gary.engine_note: tried to use None, which isn't in garys_house

donna.thought_process: Rosa and Hal both just spoke to me. Rosa wants a yes and deviled eggs for Friday at six, and Hal wants the street-facing flamingos down to three. I already hid the extras behind the hedge, so I can answer both at once and keep the peace. A firm yes to Rosa and a promise on the count keeps everyone's trust. Then I can get back to working on Gary and the pickleball ladder.

parameters.content: Yes, Rosa, wild horses couldn't keep me away, and the deviled eggs are a done deal. And Hal, dear, the extra flamingos are behind the hedge as we speak, so you can stop counting and just bring your appetite.

hal.thought_process: Rosa and Donna are sorting out Friday dinner, and I've already said my piece to Donna about the flamingos. No sense nagging again; Donna knows my terms. The flock is right here and I came out for a count anyway. A by-the-book man verifies instead of guessing. I'll tally the birds visible from the street and compare to the three-ornament limit, then decide if a report is even needed.

parameters.content: Count the street-visible flamingos against the three-ornament limit

rosa.thought_process: Donna asked what to bring, and Hal just poked her about the flamingos. I already asked her for deviled eggs last tick, so I shouldn't repeat that. Best move is to answer her question simply, confirm the plan, and keep the peace between her and Hal so the table stays friendly. Also, her dinner-is-tonight line is a little off since it's Saturday and dinner is Friday at six, so I'll gently set her straight without making a fuss.

parameters.content: Deviled eggs, Donna, that's all I need. Just you and those eggs at my table Friday at six, I've got the rest. And don't let Hal rattle you about the flamingos, we'll sort that out over supper.

laws.title: Cart Modifications
laws.text: Exterior golf cart modifications visible from the street require Architectural Review approval.

laws.title: Lawn Ornaments
laws.text: No more than 3 decorative ornaments may be visible from the street.

laws.title: Quiet Hours
laws.text: No amplified sound from 10 PM to 7 AM.

laws.title: Holiday Decor
laws.text: Holiday lighting is permitted from Thanksgiving through January 15.

laws.title: Court Reservations
laws.text: Pickleball courts may be reserved for a maximum of 2 hours per party.

laws.title: Parking
laws.text: No parking on the grass. Carts and cars stay on driveways or the street.
